default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-498.title: EMA z-score stretch fade
E-498.hypothesis: A close several standard deviations from its own session EMA is a liquidity-driven stretch by an impatient taker; passive liquidity should pull it back toward the mean.

E-499.title: US-cash-open impulse follow
E-499.hypothesis: When US equities open (10:30 or 11:30 São Paulo depending on DST) foreign flow hits the index; the first minutes' direction should carry as hedgers and index arbitrageurs follow.

E-500.title: Day-open recross after an excursion
E-500.hypothesis: After an unusually large excursion from the session open, a close back through the open means the day's initiators lost; the other side takes control.

E-501.title: Prior-session midpoint cross follow
E-501.hypothesis: The prior session's range midpoint splits yesterday's value in two; a close across it shifts the balance and the move should extend as range traders reposition.

E-502.title: Volatility-expansion direction follow
E-502.hypothesis: When recent bar ranges jump over the last hour's average, informed urgency has arrived; the net direction of that burst tends to carry while slower participants chase.

E-503.title: Higher-high higher-low ladder follow
E-503.hypothesis: Consecutive bars each making higher highs and higher lows (or the reverse) show trapped counterparties covering step by step; follow the staircase.

E-504.title: Opening-range midpoint cross follow
E-504.hypothesis: After the opening range is set, the midpoint is where early buyers and sellers balance; a close across it signals the winning side and should extend.

E-505.title: Keltner channel break follow
E-505.hypothesis: A close beyond EMA plus a multiple of average bar range signals a volatility-adjusted breakout; stop orders and momentum followers feed the move.

E-506.title: Same-minute seasonal drift follow
E-506.hypothesis: Scheduled flows (funds, hedgers, index rebalance, data releases) recur at the same clock minute; if the last 20 sessions showed a consistent bar direction at this minute, join it.

E-507.title: Chaikin money-flow zero-zone cross follow
E-507.hypothesis: Where bars close inside their range, weighted by volume, reveals who is absorbing; a flip of this flow beyond a threshold shows a new aggressor.
